_about: RATIFIED Company Standard SLA-CREDIT-REMEDY-SLA-001 (AM-193, 2026-10-26). The position is Legal
Constitution §11's Company Position under both published SLAs, quoted verbatim below: service
credits are the exclusive remedy for service interruptions, issued as a credit note against future
bills. Ratified with every Constitution position by AM-73; nothing in it is authored. A customer
MOU (2026-10-26) paid a pro-rata credit per trouble ticket, made SLA credits 'also payable' on top,
refunded accrued credits in cash on termination and called the remedy a 'Penalty' — none of which
any check read. PRESENCE: the evaluator reads no clause text; a clause that states one of the
configured waiver phrases addresses the remedy by departing from it, a DEVIATION for a person.
It is CONFIGURATION: no locked decision is amended.
description: Service credits are the only remedy for service interruptions, given as a credit against future bills.
source_document: Legal Mind — Legal Constitution, Lawyer Review Version L1.14 (docs/02-legal-domain/LEGAL_CONSTITUTION_L1.14.md)
source_quote: service credits are the exclusive remedy for service interruptions and related claims

configuration.position_statement: Under both SLAs: service credits are the exclusive remedy for service interruptions and related claims; a confirmed credit is issued within forty-five (45) days of confirmation, as a credit note against future bills for the same service.
waiver_patterns: on a prorated basis from the day
configuration._waiver_note: AM-193: recognition terms (35.4) for the ways a paper departs from §11's exclusive credit-note remedy — credits on top of another remedy, credits paid in cash, a 'penalty', a pro-rata credit per ticket. None states a position; the position is the verbatim §11 sentence above.

evaluation_rules._note: presence is established by the mapping layer alone (45D); the evaluator reads no clause text

_terminology: Mapping terminology, ratified with the standard on 2026-10-26. Only the position's own wording
('sole and exclusive remedy', 'exclusive remedy for', 'credit note against future') STATES it; 'service credit'
merely names the subject (a definition clause is no statement of the remedy) and is an alias. No term encodes a
legal position (rules 7/21). Waiver phrases name credits, a penalty or a pro-rata charge — never a general
'without prejudice to any other remedies', which every boilerplate remedies clause says. confirm_threshold 5.
